specification.title: A unique violation is caught inside the transaction, which then ends normally
steps: Start a transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API.
Write the marker `tx`, and make sure the write was sent to PostgreSQL.
Checkpoint `after-write`: report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid(), read through the transaction's own connection.

Insert the value 'taken' into uniq through the framework's ordinary write API. It fails with unique_violation (23505). Catch the error and continue. After catching the error, the callback sends nothing else and returns.
Checkpoint `before-end`: report the same backend PID. The transaction is aborted, so it cannot run queries; the runner confirms the aborted state server-side.
End the transaction normally, so that the framework sends COMMIT.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: When PostgreSQL has aborted the transaction before it ends, so that its COMMIT is answered with ROLLBACK, the API does not report a successful commit.

execution.description: Positive control. BeginTransactionAsync, parameterized commands, CommitAsync or RollbackAsync. CommitAsync is reported as committed only when a prior SELECT 1 succeeded. A 25P02 from that probe, followed by CommitAsync returning, is reported as rolled_back. The command tag is not read. A thrown CommitAsync is reported as failed and the connection is disposed. A failed RollbackAsync(savepoint) is followed by RollbackAsync, not CommitAsync. A thrown RollbackAsync disposes the connection. IsolationLevel is passed to BeginTransactionAsync. Pooling is off.

configuration.commit_outcome: CommitAsync after SELECT 1; rolled_back when the probe failed with 25P02; the command tag is not read

execution.form: NpgsqlConnection.BeginTransactionAsync, parameterized commands, then CommitAsync or RollbackAsync. One connection is held until the case's after-end checkpoint, unless the policy disposed it.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A unique_violation raised by PostgreSQL inside the transaction, and caught by the application.
fault.injection_point: After the first write, before the transaction ends.
fault.preconditions: The row 'taken' already exists in uniq (fixture).
fault.expected_server: The failed statement aborts the transaction. PostgreSQL answers the later COMMIT with the command tag ROLLBACK, without an error, and commits nothing.
fault.expected_client: The driver receives the command tag ROLLBACK as the reply to COMMIT.

knowledge: The outcome reaches the client: PostgreSQL's reply to COMMIT carries the command tag ROLLBACK.

api_outcome.basis: SELECT 1 failed with 25P02 before CommitAsync, and CommitAsync then returned. 25P02 means the session is in a failed transaction block. Npgsql 10.0.3 CommitAsync does not expose the command tag. The policy reports rolled_back from the 25P02, not from a tag it did not read.
api_outcome.contract: The correct npgsql-control policy uses NpgsqlConnection.BeginTransactionAsync, NpgsqlTransaction.CommitAsync, RollbackAsync, SaveAsync, RollbackAsync(name), and ReleaseAsync. Npgsql 10.0.3 CommitAsync sends COMMIT and waits for CommandComplete and ReadyForQuery. ExecuteInternalCommand does not read the command tag. TransactionStatus on the connector is internal and is Idle after both a committed transaction and a COMMIT that PostgreSQL answered with ROLLBACK. The public transaction API does not expose either fact. Before CommitAsync the policy runs SELECT 1 on the same connection. SQLSTATE 25P02 means the session is in a failed transaction block. If that probe fails with 25P02 and CommitAsync returns, the policy reports rolled_back and says it did not read the tag. If the probe succeeds and CommitAsync returns, the policy reports committed. A return from CommitAsync with no probe is not reported as a commit. If CommitAsync throws, the policy reports failed and disposes the connection. If RollbackAsync throws, it disposes the connection and does not call CommitAsync. A failed RollbackAsync(savepoint) is followed by RollbackAsync of the surrounding transaction. IsolationLevel is passed to BeginTransactionAsync.

preconditions.description: the write of marker "tx" had reached PostgreSQL at `after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the duplicate insert failed with unique_violation (23505), as reported by the adapter
the top-level transaction was aborted before it ended: at `before-end` the session was "idle in transaction (aborted)" and pg_xact_status() already reported it aborted
PostgreSQL did not commit the transaction
